source: Lyman, Balmer and Paschen lines follow 1/λ = R(1/n_f² − 1/n_i²).
Students swap n_f and n_i, getting a negative wavelength or the wrong series.

Hydrogen's emission spectrum is a set of sharp lines that fall into families, or series, each named for its discoverer. With the Bohr energies, every line has a simple label: the level the electron starts in and the level it lands in.

A drop from level $n_i$ to a lower level $n_f$ emits a photon with $$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H\left(\frac{1}{n_f^2} - \frac{1}{n_i^2}\right),\qquad R_H = 1.097 \times 10^7\ \text{m}^{-1}.$$ The series are set by $n_f$: Lyman ($n_f = 1$, ultraviolet), Balmer ($n_f = 2$, visible and near UV), Paschen ($n_f = 3$, infrared). Letting $n_i \to \infty$ gives each series' shortest wavelength, its limit.

The photon carries away the energy difference: $\frac{hc}{\lambda} = E_{n_i} - E_{n_f} = 13.6\ \text{eV}\left(\frac{1}{n_f^2} - \frac{1}{n_i^2}\right)$. Divide by $hc$: $R = \frac{13.6\ \text{eV}}{1240\ \text{eV·nm}} = 0.01097\ \text{nm}^{-1} = 1.097 \times 10^7\ \text{m}^{-1}$. Johann Balmer found the pattern of the visible lines by trial in 1885; Bohr's model explained it. Because $n_i > n_f$, the bracket is positive, and the lines of a series crowd together toward the limit as $n_i$ grows.
Hydrogen's levels with three Balmer jumps (to $n = 2$) and the first Lyman jump (to $n = 1$). The Lyman jump is far larger, so its photon is ultraviolet.

Astronomers use these lines every day. The red Balmer line (656 nm) gives glowing hydrogen clouds around young stars their pink-red color, and the Lyman-alpha line (121.6 nm, ultraviolet), stretched by the expansion of the universe into visible or infrared light, is one of the main ways the most distant galaxies are found.

Swapping $n_f$ and $n_i$. Writing $\frac{1}{n_i^2} - \frac{1}{n_f^2}$ with $n_i > n_f$ gives a negative wavelength; using the wrong level as $n_f$ puts the line in the wrong series. The lower level, where the electron lands, sets the series and goes first in the bracket. Check: Balmer lines must come out between about 365 and 656 nm.
